title: Lovász Local Lemma OQ-01: Mutual Independence Discharges the Toolkit's IndepSet Hypothesis
description: The measure-theoretic OQ-01 program has built an extensive toolkit (Independence.lean, DependencySplit.lean, ChainRule.lean) whose lemmas all take as a standing hypothesis the pairwise fact that a bad event Aᵢ is independent of the joint avoidance of some other index set: IndepSet (A i) (⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ) μ. For instance seq_indep_avoidance_eq_prod assumes ∀ n, IndepSet (A n) (⋂_{j<n} (A j)ᶜ) μ, and cond_failure_eq_measure_of_indep_subset assumes IndepSet (A i) (⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ) μ. Their docstrings note this is 'a strictly weaker, one-sided condition that mutual independence implies' — but that implication was never proved in Lean: no file derives such an IndepSet from the family-level mutual independence iIndepSet A μ. This entry supplies exactly that missing bridge, over an arbitrary index type: iIndepSet A μ → i ∉ S → IndepSet (A i) (⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ) μ. The proof routes through Mathlib's iIndepSet.indep_generateFrom_of_disjoint for the disjoint index sets {i} and S — Aᵢ is measurable in the σ-algebra generated by {Aᵢ} and the finite avoidance is measurable in the σ-algebra generated by {Aₖ : k ∈ S}, so the two are independent — then repackages the resulting measure factorization as an IndepSet term via indepSet_iff_measure_inter_eq_mul. As corollaries it re-derives the toolkit's conditional identity μ[Aᵢ | ⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ] = μ(Aᵢ) without the IndepSet hypothesis, and its chain-rule prefix specialization. This is the measure-theoretic non-neighbour step of the LLL induction in the d=0 (fully-independent) regime. 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: Fully verified: 0 sorries, 0 axiom declarations, no structure-encoded assumptions, no native_decide/decide (only foundational propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound from the Mathlib probability lemmas used — confirmed by #print axioms on all four theorems). Scope: this entry proves that the family-level mutual independence iIndepSet A μ implies, for i ∉ S, the pairwise independence IndepSet (A i) (⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ) μ — the standing hypothesis that the rest of the OQ-01 measure-theoretic toolkit assumes but had never derived. It does NOT prove the general bounded-dependency-degree LLL (that a dependency structure with e·p·(d+1) ≤ 1 forces positive avoidance): that induction, which requires bounding conditional failure probabilities across the dependency graph, remains the open OQ-01 research target. What this entry adds is the verified reduction from mutual independence to the per-event/avoidance IndepSet input, which makes the existing sequential and subset-history developments run directly from iIndepSet A μ.
originalContributions: indepSet_avoidance (flagship): iIndepSet A μ → i ∉ S → IndepSet (A i) (⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ) μ. The bridge from family-level mutual independence to the pairwise event-vs-avoidance independence that the OQ-01 toolkit (seq_indep_avoidance_eq_prod, cond_failure_eq_measure_of_indep_subset, ...) takes as an unproven hypothesis. Nothing in the program previously derived such an IndepSet from iIndepSet; this closes that gap over an arbitrary index type.

indep_avoidance: the raw measure factorization μ(A i ∩ ⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ) = μ(A i) · μ(⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ) for i ∉ S. Routes through iIndepSet.indep_generateFrom_of_disjoint for the disjoint index sets {i} and ↑S, extracting the intersection-measure identity from the σ-algebra independence via Indep_iff. The measurability side-goals are discharged by measurableSet_generateFrom (for A i) and Finset.measurableSet_biInter of complements (for the avoidance set), both taken in the generated σ-algebras.

cond_avoidance_eq_self: μ[A i | ⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ] = μ(A i) for i ∉ S, given the avoidance has positive measure. This is the OQ-01 toolkit's conditional identity cond_failure_eq_measure_of_indep_subset with its IndepSet hypothesis discharged by the bridge above — it now follows directly from iIndepSet A μ, with no standalone independence assumption. The measure-theoretic d=0 non-neighbour step of the LLL induction.

cond_prefix_eq_self: the chain-rule prefix specialization over a linear order — conditioning A k on the avoidance of all strictly earlier events leaves its probability unchanged. This certifies that the chain-rule per-event failure probability bₖ = μ[A k | ⋂_{j<k} (A j)ᶜ] collapses to the unconditional μ(A k) in the independent regime, so the quantitative bound ∏(1 − bₖ) recovers the exact base-case factorization ∏(1 − μ(A k)) — now from iIndepSet A μ alone.

Framing contribution: the OQ-01 measure-theoretic toolkit was built modularly, each piece assuming the per-event/avoidance IndepSet as a hypothesis, with the derivation from mutual independence deferred. This entry supplies that deferred derivation, so the whole sequential/subset development is now grounded in the single hypothesis iIndepSet A μ.

overview.historicalContext: The Lovász Local Lemma (Erdős–Lovász, 1975) proves that if each bad event Aᵢ is mutually independent of all but a bounded number d of the others and each has probability p with e·p·(d+1) ≤ 1, then all events can be avoided simultaneously with positive probability. The standard proof (Spencer's exposition of Erdős–Lovász) proceeds by induction, bounding conditional probabilities μ[Aᵢ | ⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ] over subsets S of the other events, and splits S into neighbours and non-neighbours of i in the dependency graph. The non-neighbour part rests on a single measure-theoretic fact: conditioning on the avoidance of events that are independent of Aᵢ does not change Aᵢ's probability. In the fully-independent (d=0) regime every other event is a non-neighbour, so this fact holds unconditionally. The OQ-01 measure-theoretic program in this gallery has built the surrounding machinery — the chain-rule factorization of avoidance into conditional survivals, monotonicity and numerator/denominator peels for the dependency split, and exact avoidance products under sequential independence — but each of those pieces assumed the pairwise independence IndepSet (A i) (⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ) μ as a hypothesis. This entry proves that hypothesis follows from full mutual independence iIndepSet A μ, using Mathlib's σ-algebra independence API for disjoint index sets.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open question OQ-01 (from LovaszLocalLemma.lean)**: formalize the full probabilistic Lovász Local Lemma over measure-theoretic probability spaces.

**This entry (independence bridge)**: prove that family-level mutual independence discharges the pairwise IndepSet hypothesis assumed throughout the OQ-01 toolkit. For a measurable family A : ι → Set Ω with iIndepSet A μ and any i ∉ S (S : Finset ι), the event A i is independent of the joint avoidance ⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ, giving both the measure factorization μ(A i ∩ ⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ) = μ(A i)·μ(⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ) and, when the avoidance has positive measure, the conditional identity μ[A i | ⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ] = μ(A i).
overview.text: Every proof of the Lovász Local Lemma leans on one intuitive fact: if a bad event has nothing to do with a bunch of other events, then hearing that all those others were avoided tells you nothing about it — its probability is unchanged. When the whole family is mutually independent this holds for any collection of 'other' events at once. The surrounding formal toolkit for this problem had been quietly assuming this fact event-by-event; this entry proves it once and for all from mutual independence, so the rest of the development no longer has to take it on faith.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Reduce to σ-algebra independence.** Mathlib's iIndepSet.indep_generateFrom_of_disjoint states that for a mutually independent family and disjoint index sets S, T, the σ-algebras generated by {Aₙ : n∈S} and {Aₖ : k∈T} are independent. Instantiate with the disjoint singleton {i} and the finite set ↑S (disjoint because i ∉ S).

**Locate the events in those σ-algebras.** A i is measurable in generateFrom {A i} (measurableSet_generateFrom on the singleton membership). Each complement (A j)ᶜ, j∈S, is measurable in generateFrom {Aₖ : k∈S} (membership witnessed by ⟨j, j∈S, rfl⟩, then .compl), and the finite intersection ⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ is measurable there by Finset.measurableSet_biInter.

**Extract the measure identity.** Indep_iff turns the σ-algebra independence into μ(A i ∩ ⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ) = μ(A i)·μ(⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ) (theorem indep_avoidance). indepSet_iff_measure_inter_eq_mul repackages this as IndepSet (A i) (⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ) μ (theorem indepSet_avoidance).

**Conditional corollary.** cond_apply' unfolds μ[A i | H] = (μ H)⁻¹·μ(H ∩ A i); after Set.inter_comm and the factorization, ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel (using μ H ≠ 0 and μ H ≠ ∞, the latter from the derived IsProbabilityMeasure) collapses it to μ(A i) (theorem cond_avoidance_eq_self). The prefix version cond_prefix_eq_self specialises S to a set of strictly-earlier indices over a linear order.
keyInsights: The whole content is a bridge between two Mathlib notions of independence: iIndepSet (a family is mutually independent) and IndepSet (two specific sets are independent). The key API is iIndepSet.indep_generateFrom_of_disjoint, which lifts family independence to independence of the σ-algebras generated by disjoint index sets; the finite avoidance ⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ lives in one of those σ-algebras because it is a finite intersection of complements of generators.

The OQ-01 toolkit was deliberately modular: DependencySplit and Independence lemmas assume IndepSet (A i) (⋂ Aⱼᶜ) μ so they can be proved without committing to how that independence arises. That design left a real gap — the assumption was justified only in prose ('mutual independence implies it'). This entry converts that prose into a proof, retroactively grounding every hypothesis-carrying lemma of the program in iIndepSet A μ.

In the d=0 (fully-independent) regime the dependency-graph neighbourhood of every event is empty, so the LLL's non-neighbour reduction becomes the entire step: conditioning on the avoidance of ALL other events leaves a probability unchanged. This is why indepSet_avoidance holds for an arbitrary index subset S, not just a designated non-neighbour set — there are no neighbours to exclude.

The conditional identity requires the conditioning avoidance to have positive measure; this is automatic in the LLL because the base case (LovaszLocalLemmaOQ01.lean) proves μ(⋂ Aⱼᶜ) > 0 under μ(Aⱼ) < 1. Keeping μ(⋂ Aⱼᶜ) ≠ 0 as an explicit hypothesis here keeps the bridge lemma independent of any particular positivity route.

The disjoint-index-set factorization is the crux, not the IndepSet repackaging. The real work is indep_avoidance: mutual independence iIndepSet A μ gives independence of the σ-algebras generated by DISJOINT index sets (iIndepSet.indep_generateFrom_of_disjoint), and the finite avoidance ⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ qualifies because it is a finite intersection of complements of generators, hence measurable in generateFrom {A k : k∈S}. Once that measure identity μ(Aᵢ ∩ H) = μ(Aᵢ)·μ(H) is in hand, both the IndepSet packaging (indepSet_avoidance) and the conditional corollary (cond_avoidance_eq_self) are one lemma-application away — so the entire bridge rests on correctly matching Mathlib's disjoint-generateFrom independence to the avoidance set's σ-algebra membership.

As corollaries the toolkit's conditional identity μ[A i | ⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ] = μ(A i) and its chain-rule prefix form follow directly from mutual independence. Fully checked: 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications:
**Grounds the OQ-01 toolkit in a single hypothesis.** The sequential-independence results (seq_indep_avoidance_eq_prod, seq_indep_avoidance_pos, seq_indep_avoidance_ge_pow in Independence.lean) and the subset-history lemmas (cond_failure_eq_measure_of_indep_subset in DependencySplit.lean) all assumed a per-event/avoidance IndepSet. This entry derives that IndepSet from iIndepSet A μ, so those developments can be instantiated from mutual independence alone — the honest first *conditional* step of the LLL induction beyond the base-case factorization.

**Honest scope**: this is the d=0 (fully-independent) instance of the LLL's non-neighbour reduction. It does NOT prove the bounded-dependency-degree induction (deriving the per-event conditional bounds μ[Aᵢ | ⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ] ≤ xᵢ across a dependency graph under e·p·(d+1) ≤ 1), which needs the neighbour split and the denominator recursion and remains the open OQ-01 research target. What this entry closes is the gap between the family independence hypothesis and the pairwise independence the rest of the toolkit consumes.
openQuestions: Generalise the bridge to the dependency-graph setting: replace mutual independence iIndepSet with 'Aᵢ is mutually independent of {Aⱼ : j ∉ Γ(i)}', and derive IndepSet (A i) (⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ) μ only for S disjoint from the neighbourhood Γ(i) — the actual non-neighbour hypothesis of the general LLL.

Combine indepSet_avoidance with the DependencySplit numerator bound and the DenominatorStep survival peel to prove the inductive claim μ[Aᵢ | ⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ] ≤ xᵢ by induction on |S|, the missing core of the bounded-degree LLL.

Feed indepSet_avoidance into seq_indep_avoidance_eq_prod to obtain a second, chain-rule-based derivation of the exact avoidance product μ(⋂ Aᵢᶜ) = ∏(1 − μ(Aᵢ)) from iIndepSet A μ, and verify it agrees with the direct meas_iInter derivation of the base case lovasz-local-lemma-oq-01.

crossReferences.description: The d=0 base case, which proves the exact avoidance factorization μ(⋂ Aᵢᶜ) = ∏(1 − μ(Aᵢ)) and positive avoidance directly from iIndepSet A μ. This entry adds the first *conditional* consequence of that same mutual-independence hypothesis: conditioning on the avoidance of a disjoint index set leaves an event's probability unchanged.

The subset-history toolkit whose cond_failure_eq_measure_of_indep_subset assumes IndepSet (A i) (⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ) μ. This entry derives exactly that IndepSet from iIndepSet A μ, discharging the hypothesis so the dependency-split collapse μ[Aᵢ | ⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ] = μ(Aᵢ) follows from mutual independence.

The chain-rule scaffold consuming per-event conditional failure probabilities bₖ = μ[A k | ⋂_{j<k} Aⱼᶜ]. cond_prefix_eq_self here certifies that in the independent regime bₖ = μ(A k), so the chain-rule quantitative bound reproduces the exact base-case factorization.
